campaign: V1 Phase B B.6''.9.8.5b.2 - actuator substitution semantics audit (READ-ONLY)
purpose: Determine whether Marlin/VOLT/Koopman use per-CUfunction-lifetime (static) or per-launch (dynamic) substitution. Answer dictates which fix (Option A/B/C) is correct for .8.5b SEGV.

section_a_marlin_substitution_semantics.registration_pattern: cipher_rt_matmul_register_actuator(&g_marlin_actuator) — registers as cuBLAS-layer actuator on the cipher_rt_matmul_dispatch substrate
section_a_marlin_substitution_semantics.dispatch_layer: cuBLAS shim (cipher_rt_cublasGemmEx_impl in cipher_rt_cublas_shim.c) — NOT cuLaunchKernel hook
decision_inputs: call->m/n/k (M/N/K shape gates: M<=64, N/K>=1024, K%128==0, N%64==0)
weight pointer stability count (cipher_rt_marlin_engine_observe_weight, lazy quantization on first stability hit)
TLS substitute_hint from classify observer (LIVE=0 advisory, LIVE=1 binding)
section_a_marlin_substitution_semantics.decision_classification: PER-cublasGemmEx-CALL (per-launch within cuBLAS, but at cuBLAS layer not CUfunction layer)
section_a_marlin_substitution_semantics.substitution_target: cipher_rt_marlin_engine_dispatch(call->B, marlin_B, marlin_S, call->C, ...) — REPLACES the cublasGemmEx call entirely with own marlin GEMM kernel dispatched via cuLaunchKernel
section_a_marlin_substitution_semantics.graph_mode_compose: When PyTorch is in graph capture mode and calls cublasGemmEx, cipher_rt_phase4's GOT-patched cublasGemmEx fires → Marlin's maybe_handle decides → Marlin dispatches its kernel via cuLaunchKernel → driver records the Marlin kernel as a graph node (PyTorch's normal capture mechanism). Graph replay runs Marlin natively. NO per-launch substitution hook needed.
section_a_marlin_substitution_semantics.ed_to_support_marlin_via_option_a_b_c: ZERO — Marlin already works under PyTorch graph mode through the cuBLAS-layer mechanism

section_b_koopman_substitution_semantics.registration_pattern: same as Marlin — cipher_rt_matmul_register_actuator(&g_koopman_actuator) on cuBLAS-layer substrate
decision_inputs: OOD detector: cipher_koopman_fp16_ood_max_residual(call->B, M, K_dim, N_dim) computes residual_ratio = ||x - V_x V_x^T x|| / ||x||
shape registry membership (cipher_koopman_fp16_launch_shape returns -1 if shape not registered)
section_b_koopman_substitution_semantics.decision_classification: PER-cublasGemmEx-CALL with PER-LAUNCH input-dependent β residual_ratio gate (Memory #13 OOD detector)
section_b_koopman_substitution_semantics.substitution_target: cipher_koopman_fp16_launch_shape(call->B, call->C, M, K_dim, N_dim) — narrow-domain O(1) surrogate kernel
section_b_koopman_substitution_semantics.memory_13_beta_gate_per_launch: TRUE — residual_ratio is recomputed per cublasGemmEx call on call->B input data. This is INTRINSICALLY dynamic per-launch.
section_b_koopman_substitution_semantics.graph_mode_compose: Same as Marlin — cuBLAS-layer interception fires under graph capture; Koopman kernel dispatched via cuLaunchKernel; recorded into graph; replay runs natively. However, the OOD β gate is decided at CAPTURE TIME based on the input data at capture; replay uses captured topology regardless of new input data. This means: cross-distribution inputs at replay time bypass the OOD gate (incorrect substitution applied to OOD input). This is a SEPARATE problem not addressable by graph-time substitution shims; needs graph re-capture on OOD detection or pre-launch OOD check that triggers graph rebuild.
section_b_koopman_substitution_semantics.ed_to_support_koopman_via_option_a_b_c: ZERO for the in-distribution capture case (works via cuBLAS layer). Cross-distribution input correctness at replay is a separate v1.x concern requiring graph invalidation logic — not Option A/B/C scope.
section_b_koopman_substitution_semantics.honest_constraint: Koopman correctness under graph mode requires that input distributions don't drift across graph replays. If drift occurs, captured Koopman substitution may apply OOD substitution to a now-OOD input. v1.x mitigation: pre-replay OOD check + graph invalidation. Not B.6''.9.8 scope.

section_c_volt_semantics.registration_pattern: Init-time ONLY (cipher_rt_volt_init called from cipher_inject.c). No per-launch hook.
section_c_volt_semantics.dispatch_layer: NONE — VOLT is one-shot NVML clock-lock applied at libcipher_rt init
section_c_volt_semantics.explicit_quote_from_header: 'v1 scope: env-driven static clock lock via nvmlDeviceSetGpuLockedClocks applied at libcipher_rt init, restored at exit (atexit + signal handlers). No per-launch classifier in v1; that's T4.3.2 once cuBLAS interception or kernel-name-based shape inference is in place.'
section_c_volt_semantics.graph_mode_compose: VOLT operates orthogonally — clock lock affects all kernels including graph-captured ones. No interaction with capture/replay.
section_c_volt_semantics.ed_to_support_volt_via_option_a_b_c: ZERO — VOLT doesn't need launch-time hook at all

section_d_recommendation.headline_finding: ALL THREE CURRENT ACTUATORS (Marlin, Koopman, VOLT) do NOT use cipher_rt_graph_substitute_decide. They operate at cuBLAS-layer (Marlin/Koopman) or init-layer (VOLT). The cuLaunchKernel substitution hook the .8.5 + .8.5b substeps wired is solving a problem that does not exist in v1's actuator architecture.
implications: B.6''.9.8.5 explicit cuGraphAddKernelNode substitution shims: still useful for direct-CUDA-API callers (raw CUDA, HPC, JAX direct) but NO v1 actuator wires them
B.6''.9.8.5b cuLaunchKernel-during-capture substitution: solves no v1 problem; the SEGV is in a code path no v1 actuator exercises
The weak hook cipher_rt_graph_substitute_decide is FUTURE-proofing for hypothetical CUfunction-level actuators (none in v1)

For FlashAttention (B.6''.9.8.6 next substep): FlashAttention calls its own kernels via cuLaunchKernel from the flash_attn Python module. Substitution there would NEED some CUfunction-level mechanism, but the actuator implementation is downstream (v1.x or later); the substrate hook should be designed when the actuator is.

options_ranked_for_the_FUTURE_per_kernel.option: C — registration-time substitution at cuModuleGetFunction / cuKernelGetFunction
options_ranked_for_the_FUTURE_per_kernel.mechanism: When framework resolves a kernel handle via cuModuleGetFunction, our shim can return a substitute CUfunction. ALL subsequent uses (cuLaunchKernel, cuGraphAddKernelNode, graph capture) use the substituted handle automatically.
pros: Zero per-launch overhead (substitution decision made once at registration)
Zero SEGV class (no cuStreamGetCaptureInfo needed; no cross-TU TLS coordination)
Framework-agnostic (works for direct CUDA, PyTorch, JAX, HPC equally)
Composes cleanly with graph capture (substitute handle gets recorded as graph node)
Memory #20 ABI-additive (existing cuModuleGetFunction shim already exists from .8.1)
cons: Substitution decision must be made before per-launch input data is available — rules out OOD-gated substitution like Koopman's β check (but Koopman uses cuBLAS layer anyway)
Requires substitute kernel to be ABI-compatible across ALL future calls of that kernel
options_ranked_for_the_FUTURE_per_kernel.ed_to_implement: ~0.75-1 ED (extend existing cuModuleGetFunction shim with substitute decision hook; remove .8.5 + .8.5b cuGraph + cuStreamGetCaptureInfo paths)

options_ranked_for_the_FUTURE_per_kernel.option: A — per-stream capture-state cache via cuStreamBeginCapture hook
options_ranked_for_the_FUTURE_per_kernel.mechanism: Maintain shadow set of capturing streams; check membership instead of calling cuStreamGetCaptureInfo per launch.
pros: Per-launch input data IS available for OOD-gated decisions
cons: Per-launch overhead even if cheap (set membership check + branch)
Still requires substitute kernel ABI-compat per launch

options_ranked_for_the_FUTURE_per_kernel.option: B — extern __thread cipher_in_cublas_inflight cross-TU shared marker
options_ranked_for_the_FUTURE_per_kernel.mechanism: Patch cipher_rt_cublas_shim.c to set TLS marker around real cuBLAS calls; may13 helper checks it.
cons: Doesn't generalize to OTHER SEGV sources (e.g., cuDNN-internal launches)

section_d_recommendation.recommendation: OPTION C (registration-time substitution at cuModuleGetFunction). For v1's actuator architecture, Option C is correct because: (1) Marlin/Koopman work at cuBLAS layer — no kernel-substitution hook needed there; (2) future per-CUfunction actuators (e.g., FlashAttention substitution in v1.x) are best served by registration-time decisions, not per-launch decisions; (3) zero SEGV class; (4) zero per-launch overhead; (5) ABI-additive.

section_e_refined_ed_estimate.step_1_rollback_8_5b_cuStreamGetCaptureI: 0.25 ED — remove env-gated capture-detect helper + cuStreamGetCaptureInfo resolver from cipher_intercept_cudart.cpp. KEEP the .8.5 shims (cuGraphAddKernelNode + cuGraphExecKernelNodeSetParams + cudaGraphAddKernelNode) for direct-API callers.
section_e_refined_ed_estimate.step_2_extend_cuModuleGetFunction_shim_w: 0.5 ED — add weak ref cipher_rt_kernel_substitute_decide(CUmodule mod, const char* name) in existing cuModuleGetFunction shim. When non-null + returns non-NULL substitute, return substitute CUfunction instead of real.
section_e_refined_ed_estimate.step_3_apply_same_to_cuLibraryGetKernel_: 0.25 ED — parallel extension for the CUDA 12+ library API
section_e_refined_ed_estimate.step_4_build_test_correctness_gate_commi: 0.5 ED — eager parity 12/12 EXACT preserved (since no per-launch path touched); graph mode unchanged
section_e_refined_ed_estimate.comparison_to_8_5b_already_spent: 1.5 ED on .8.5b; ~0.5 ED to roll back + 1.5 ED for Option C = 2 ED net; vs Option A 2-3 ED additional with no rollback. Option C still cheaper end-to-end.

section_v1_x_actuator_carries: Marlin + Koopman already work in graph mode via cuBLAS-layer interception (no shim change needed)
VOLT operates orthogonally (no shim change needed)

Koopman OOD-gate-under-graph-replay correctness: input distribution drift at replay time defeats capture-time β gate. v1.x mitigation: pre-replay OOD check + graph invalidation. SEPARATE concern from .8.5b/.8.5b.2.
FlashAttention launch-side intercept (.8.6 next substep): substrate needs cuModuleGetFunction substitute hook — Option C lands the hook; FlashAttention actuator implementation is downstream
